title: Metrics and normalisation

kcs.statement: For unit vectors, cosine, dot product and Euclidean distance give identical rankings.
An unnormalised dot product favours long vectors.

misconceptions.statement: Dot product and cosine always rank the same.

parts.title: Cosine, dot product, Euclidean, and why normalization makes them agree

beats.title: Cosine, dot product, Euclidean, and why normalization makes them agree

question.prompt_md: Every vector in your index has length exactly 1. You rank the same query three ways: by **dot product**, by **cosine similarity**, and by **Euclidean distance** (smallest first). Will the top result differ?

options.md: No: all three give the same ranking
options.why_md: Right. You'll see exactly why in a moment: with unit vectors, distance is a function of cosine, and dot product equals cosine.
In general they do, but length 1 removes the only thing that separates them.
With unit vectors the agreement holds for every query.

md:
- **Cosine similarity**: the angle only. Higher means more similar.
- **Dot product**: angle *and* length. Higher means more similar.
- **Euclidean (L2) distance**: the straight-line gap. **Lower** means more similar.
They disagree in general, but here is the most useful identity in this topic. For **unit vectors** (length 1):

block.explain_md: If every vector has length 1, then the dot product **equals** cosine, and squared Euclidean distance is a **decreasing function** of cosine. So all three give **the same ranking**. That's why you normalize once at index time and then use whichever score your database computes fastest.

block.md: OpenAI's documentation states its embeddings are **normalized to length 1**, so a plain dot product gives the cosine, and cosine and Euclidean distance produce identical rankings. Other models don't normalize unless you ask (`normalize_embeddings=True` in sentence-transformers).
block.title: What providers do
Normalize, and the metrics line up
block.goal_md: The same dial with a **normalize** switch. With it on, both tips snap to the unit circle.
block.alt: Two draggable arrows from the origin plus a normalize toggle. A live readout shows dot, cosine and Euclidean distance, and whether ranking by dot would match ranking by cosine.

tasks.prompt: With normalize **off**, make the dot product larger than 4 while cosine stays below 0.5.
tasks.aha_md: A big dot product with a poor angle: length is inflating the score. In search, this is how long or “loud” documents win when they shouldn't.

tasks.prompt: Turn normalize **on** and check: does dot now equal cosine?
tasks.aha_md: With unit vectors, dot product *is* cosine. One normalization at index time makes the metric choice irrelevant for ranking.

block.title: Which score when?
rows: Default for text. Safe when you don't know whether vectors are normalized.
Vectors are normalized (then it equals cosine and is faster), or the model was trained for dot product.
Some indexes are built around L2. With normalized vectors it ranks the same as cosine.

question.prompt_md: Two **unit** vectors have cosine similarity 0.5. What is the Euclidean distance between them?

common_wrong.why_md: √2 is the distance for perpendicular unit vectors (cos = 0).

question.hint_md: Use the identity, then take a square root.

question.prompt_md: Your search ranks by **raw dot product**, and your vectors are **not normalized**. Users complain that “the same giant FAQ page shows up for everything.” Most likely cause?

options.md: That page's vector has a much larger magnitude, which inflates its dot product with every query
options.why_md: Right. Normalize the vectors (or switch to cosine) and the length advantage disappears.

options.md: The page really is relevant to everything
options.why_md: Being somewhat related to everything doesn't make it the top result everywhere. The pattern points to magnitude.

options.md: Dot product and cosine always rank the same, so it's something else
options.why_md: They only rank the same when the vectors are normalized.

recap.formula: ‖a − b‖² = 2 − 2 cos(a, b) for unit vectors
recap.pitfall: Dot product on unnormalised vectors ranks long documents first.
